sections.title: A) REFERENCE
sections.subtitle: To refer back to previously stated people / things / situations

blocks.heading: THIS / THAT / THESE / THOSE
blocks.rule: Sirven para volver a algo ya mencionado (personas, cosas o situaciones) sin repetirlo. This / these → presente (algo cercano). That / those → pasado (algo más lejano).
examples: I studied biology. **That** allowed me to work here.
I am taking an English course. **This** will give me more opportunities to find a job.
We tend to use the computer and the tablet every day. **These inventions** have changed our lives.
I conducted some interviews with many students. **Those students** who preferred answering online were the youngest.

sections.title: B) SUBSTITUTION
sections.subtitle: A number of words that can be used to avoid repetition

blocks.heading: DO / DOES / DID → sustituye a un verbo
examples: Peter didn't want to study, but I **did**. (= wanted to study)

blocks.heading: DO / DOES / DID + SO → sustituye a verbo + objeto
examples: Peter didn't buy a new car, but I **did so**. (= bought a new car)
blocks.tip: Sale mucho en el ejercicio de completar huecos.

blocks.heading: SO / NOR / NEITHER + AUX + SUJETO
formulas: NOR / NEITHER + AUX + SUJETO (= me neither)
blocks.rule: El auxiliar depende del tiempo de la primera frase.
examples: I can play the piano. — **So can I**.
I went to the cinema. — **So did I**.
I didn't study French. — **Neither / Nor did I**.

wrong.bad: I didn't study French. — Neither didn't I.
wrong.good: I didn't study French. — Neither did I. (neither ya es negativo)

blocks.heading: SO / NOT → sustituyen a una oración con THAT después de ciertos verbos
formulas: think / expect / hope / seem / suppose / believe + SO
hope + NOT  ·  DON'T + think / expect / suppose / believe + SO
blocks.rule: So sustituye a la oración afirmativa (that I will pass the test). Para la negativa, la mayoría de estos verbos se niegan con don't (I don't think so); con hope se usa not (I hope not). Con expect también se puede usar not.
examples: Are you going to pass the test? — I **hope so**. (= that I will pass the test)
Is it going to rain? — I **expect not**.
Will it be expensive? — I **don't think so**.

wrong.bad: Is it going to rain? — I don't hope so.
wrong.good: Is it going to rain? — I hope not.

blocks.heading: IF SO / IF NOT → sustituyen a una oración entera
formulas: IF NOT = si no es así
examples: Are you free tomorrow? **If so**, we can go to the cinema. (= If you are free tomorrow)
**If not**, we can meet up another day.
blocks.tip: Speaking (Part 3): Do you think this is a good point to talk about first? If so, we can start talking about this.

blocks.heading: ONE / ONES → sustituyen a sustantivos contables
examples: I've bought a new car. — Are you talking about **the one** that is parked outside?
I have many books. **The ones** on the table are mine.
The project is by far the most interesting **one** that I've ever done.

blocks.heading: AND / BUT → se omite el sujeto / adjetivo
examples: I saw a film and **(I)** enjoyed it.
I took a test, but **(I)** didn't pass it.
Peter was tired, but I wasn't **(tired)**.

blocks.heading: Pronombre relativo como objeto directo de una defining relative clause
examples: The house **(that / which)** Peter painted is mine.

blocks.heading: El verbo principal se puede omitir después de un auxiliar
examples: Have you finished working? — Yes, I **have**.
Can you play the piano? — Yes, I **can**.

blocks.heading: MODAL + BE · MODAL + HAVE (BEEN)
formulas: MODAL + BE (presente, con el verbo to be)
MODAL + HAVE BEEN (pasado, con el verbo to be)
MODAL + HAVE (pasado, sin el verbo to be)
examples: Is Javi at home? — Yes, he **must be**.
He wasn't expelled, but he **should have been**.
Did Peter paint his house? — He **may have**.

speaking.structure: 'I think [opinion].' — 'So do I. / Neither do I.'
speaking.example: 'I don't think we should spend more money on roads.' — 'Neither do I.'

speaking.structure: I certainly hope SO / NOT. · I don't think SO. · I expect NOT.
speaking.example: Will AI replace teachers? I certainly hope not, and I don't think so, to be honest.
speaking.translation: Espero que sí / que no. · No lo creo. · Supongo que no.

speaking.structure: Do you think [option] is a good point to talk about first? If so, we can start with it. If not, ...
speaking.example: Do you think technology is a good point to talk about first? If so, we can start talking about this. If not, we could begin with education.
speaking.translation: ¿Crees que [opción] es un buen punto para empezar? Si es así, podemos empezar por ahí. Si no, ...

speaking.structure: [Topic] is by far the most [adjective] one that I've ever [participle].
speaking.example: This project is by far the most interesting one that I've ever done.
speaking.translation: [Tema] es con diferencia el más [adjetivo] que he [participio] nunca.
